questions.question: 77 - 41 + 34 + (21 + 18) times 2 - 55 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply BODMAS: First solve the bracket (21 + 18) = 39.

Multiply the result by 2: 39 × 2 = 78.

Combine all terms: 77 − 41 + 34 + 78 − 55 = 189 − 96 = 93.

**∴ The correct answer is 93.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expression: 77 − 41 + 34 + (21 + 18) × 2 − 55

Method: BODMAS Rule

⇒ 77 − 41 + 34 + (39) × 2 − 55 ⇒ 77 − 41 + 34 + 78 − 55 ⇒ (77 + 34 + 78) − (41 + 55) ⇒ 189 − 96 ⇒ 93

**∴ The correct answer is 93.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It stands for Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. It dictates the order of operations in any mathematical expression.

Bracket Types

Brackets should be solved in the order: small brackets (), then curly brackets {}, and finally big brackets [].

Addition and Subtraction Priority

Addition and Subtraction have the same priority level and can be performed from left to right or by grouping like-signed terms.

questions.question: 91 - 56 + 78 - (31 + 23) + 45 times 2 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify operations using BODMAS: Bracket → Multiplication → Addition/Subtraction.

91 − 56 + 78 − (54) + 90

Combine positive terms: 91 + 78 + 90 = 259

Combine negative terms: 56 + 54 = 110

Net result: 259 − 110 = 149

**∴ The correct answer is 149.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expression: 91 − 56 + 78 − (31 + 23) + 45 × 2

Following the BODMAS order of operations:

⇒ 91 − 56 + 78 − 54 + 45 × 2 (Solved Bracket: 31 + 23 = 54)

⇒ 91 − 56 + 78 − 54 + 90 (Solved Multiplication: 45 × 2 = 90)

⇒ 35 + 78 − 54 + 90 (Subtraction: 91 − 56 = 35)

⇒ 113 − 54 + 90 (Addition: 35 + 78 = 113)

⇒ 59 + 90 (Subtraction: 113 − 54 = 59)

⇒ 149

**∴ The correct answer is 149.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the sequence to solve mathematical expressions: Brackets (), Of (orders/powers), Division (÷), Multiplication (×), Addition (+), and Subtraction (−).

Handling Signs

While performing addition and subtraction, grouping like-signed numbers (all positives together and all negatives together) reduces the risk of calculation errors.

Unit Digit Check

In competitive exams, verify the unit digit: 1 − 6 + 8 − 4 + 0 = −1. Since the result is positive, 10 − 1 = 9. The answer must end in 9.

questions.question: 92 - 31 + 22 { of } 2 + 38 div 2 - (29) + 13 = ?
questions.solution:

Solve using BODMAS priority: Of → Division → Addition/Subtraction.

Calculate "Of" and "Division" terms: 22 of 2 = 44 and 38 ÷ 2 = 19.

Expression becomes: 92 − 31 + 44 + 19 − 29 + 13.

Group positive and negative terms: (92 + 44 + 19 + 13) − (31 + 29) = 168 − 60.

Final result: 168 − 60 = 108.

**∴ The correct answer is 108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

92 − 31 + 22 of 2 + 38 ÷ 2 − 29 + 13

**Formula Used:**

BODMAS Rule: B (Brackets), O (Of), D (Division), M (Multiplication), A (Addition), S (Subtraction).

**Calculations:**

⇒ 92 − 31 + (22 × 2) + 38 ÷ 2 − 29 + 13

⇒ 92 − 31 + 44 + 19 − 29 + 13

⇒ 61 + 44 + 19 − 29 + 13

⇒ 105 + 19 − 29 + 13

⇒ 124 − 29 + 13

⇒ 95 + 13

⇒ 108

**∴ The correct answer is 108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS/VBODMAS Rule

This rule dictates the order of operations: Vinculum, Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Of Operator Significance

The "of" operator represents multiplication but must be solved before any division or standard multiplication in the expression.

Addition and Subtraction Priority

Addition and Subtraction have the same level of priority and should be solved from left to right or by grouping signs to avoid errors.

questions.question: M and N started a business with capital of Rs. 28,000 and Rs. 32,000 . After 4 months, M withdrew Rs. 8,000 and N added Rs. 8,000 . If at the end of the year, the profit was Rs. 54,000 , find N's share.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit Ratio M : N = (28 × 4 + 20 × 8) : (32 × 4 + 40 × 8)

⇒ 272 : 448 = 17 : 28

Total Ratio Parts = 17 + 28 = 45 units

45 units = ₹54,000 → 1 unit = ₹1,200

N's Share = 28 units × 1,200 = ₹33,600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹33,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Capital: M = ₹28,000, N = ₹32,000

After 4 months: M's Capital = 28,000 − 8,000 = ₹20,000; N's Capital = 32,000 + 8,000 = ₹40,000

Total Profit = ₹54,000, Total Time = 12 months

**Formula Used:**

Profit Ratio = (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/661d881643de67e0afbc16a0e6c46f99b8b33308aa1cabf6d4ffaa48b1a3dce0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Investment of M = (28,000 × 4) + (20,000 × 8)

⇒ M's Share = 1,12,000 + 1,60,000 = ₹2,72,000

⇒ Total Investment of N = (32,000 × 4) + (40,000 × 8)

⇒ N's Share = 1,28,000 + 3,20,000 = ₹4,48,000

⇒ Ratio of M's profit to N's profit = 2,72,000 : 4,48,000 = 17 : 28

⇒ N's share of profit = (28 ÷ (17 + 28)) × 54,000

⇒ N's share = (28 ÷ 45) × 54,000

⇒ N's share = 28 × 1,200 = ₹33,600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹33,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Partnership

When investments of all partners are for the same time, profit is distributed in the ratio of their capitals: P₁ : P₂ = C₁ : C₂.

Compound Partnership

When investments are for different time periods, profit ratio is the product of capital and time: P₁ : P₂ = (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂).

Working vs. Sleeping Partner

A working partner manages the business and may receive a fixed salary or percentage of profit before the remaining profit is divided.

questions.question: A car travels 80 { km} at 40 { km/h} , 120 { km} at 60 { km/h} , and 100 { km} at 50 { km/h} . Find the average speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Total Distance = 80 + 120 + 100 = 300 km

Total Time = (80/40) + (120/60) + (100/50) = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 hours

Average Speed = 300 ÷ 6 = 50 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance₁ (d₁) = 80 km, Speed₁ (s₁) = 40 km/h

Distance₂ (d₂) = 120 km, Speed₂ (s₂) = 60 km/h

Distance₃ (d₃) = 100 km, Speed₃ (s₃) = 50 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/359f60ac9f91cf196b8615518cd5c15cdd1157190a70637cc619405bddf98a90.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time₁ = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 hours

⇒ Time₂ = 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours

⇒ Time₃ = 100 ÷ 50 = 2 hours

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 80 + 120 + 100 = 300 km

⇒ Average Speed = 300 ÷ 6 = 50 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If a journey is divided into two equal distances traveled at speeds x and y, the average speed is 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. If they move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

questions.question: A trader sells two articles at the same selling price. On one, he makes 10\% profit, on the other, he incurs 10\% loss. What is his overall profit or loss on the entire transaction?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two articles are sold at the same price, one at x% profit and the other at x% loss, there is always an overall loss.

Shortcut formula: Overall Loss % = (x / 10)²

Given: x = 10%

Overall Loss % = (10 / 10)² = 1² = 1%

**∴ The correct answer is 1% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c4b249a8b49ea5d359fddc86e0d155d8eb1c238ac3ed85a4c36d6052243a652.png] 

Given: SP₁ = SP₂, Profit % = 10%, Loss % = 10%

Formula: CP = SP × [100 / (100 ± Profit/Loss %)]

Let the Selling Price (SP) of each article be ₹99.

⇒ CP₁ = 99 × (100 / 110) = ₹90

⇒ CP₂ = 99 × (100 / 90) = ₹110

⇒ Total CP = 90 + 110 = ₹200

⇒ Total SP = 99 + 99 = ₹198

⇒ Overall Loss = 200 − 198 = ₹2

⇒ Overall Loss % = (2 / 200) × 100 = 1%

**∴ The correct answer is 1% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equal Cost Price Case

If two articles are sold at the same Cost Price, one at x% profit and another at x% loss, the net result is always 0% (No Profit, No Loss).

Successive Percentage Formula

Net change for two successive changes of a% and b% is given by [a + b + (ab / 100)]%.

Same SP with Different %

If two items are sold at same SP with x% profit and y% loss, net % = [100(x−y) − 2xy] / [200+x−y].

questions.question: In an election contested by two candidates, 1,780 votes were declared invalid. The winning candidate secured 82\% of the valid votes and triumphed by a margin of 80 votes. Determine the total number of votes cast in the election.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Winner = 82% of Valid votes → Loser = 18% of Valid votes.

Victory Margin = 82% − 18% = 64% of Valid votes.

64% = 80 → 1% = 1.25 → 100% (Valid) = 125 votes.

Total Votes = Valid + Invalid = 125 + 1780 = 1905 votes.

**∴ The correct answer is 1905 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Invalid votes = 1,780

Winner's share = 82% of valid votes

Margin of victory = 80 votes

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6f217b12af6a7e7dbf1943db81769aa10a1529ba9bd664f54ac9caf7adc3580f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Total Valid Votes = V

⇒ Winner's Votes = 82% of V = 0.82V

⇒ Loser's Votes = (100 − 82)% of V = 18% of V = 0.18V

⇒ Margin = Winner's Votes − Loser's Votes

⇒ 80 = 0.82V − 0.18V

⇒ 80 = 0.64V

⇒ V = 80 ÷ 0.64 = 125

⇒ Total Votes Cast = Valid Votes + Invalid Votes

⇒ Total Votes Cast = 125 + 1780 = 1905

**∴ The correct answer is 1905 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Election Margin Calculation

In a two-candidate election, if the winner gets x% of votes, the margin is (x − (100 − x))% = (2x − 100)% of the total valid votes.

Valid vs Invalid Votes

Total votes cast = Valid votes + Invalid votes. Percentages are always calculated on the base of valid votes unless specified otherwise.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To simplify calculations, convert percentages to fractions: 64% = 64/100 = 16/25. Thus, (16/25) × Valid = 80 ⇒ Valid = 125.

questions.question: A triangle has sides in the ratio 3:4:5 and a perimeter of 36 cm. Find its area.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio 3 : 4 : 5 represents a right-angled triangle (Pythagorean triplet).

Sum of ratios = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts.

12 parts = 36 cm ⇒ 1 part = 3 cm.

Sides are (3 × 3) = 9 cm and (4 × 3) = 12 cm (base and height).

Area = 1/2 × 9 × 12 = 54 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 54 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Ratio of sides = 3 : 4 : 5, Perimeter = 36 cm.

Formula: Area of Right-Angled Triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8bc4d962003f7275990a74599177ac30cc1e364c13df735803058620992cfcb3.png] 

⇒ Let the sides be 3x, 4x, and 5x.

⇒ Perimeter = 3x + 4x + 5x = 36

⇒ 12x = 36

⇒ x = 3 cm

⇒ Side 1 = 3 × 3 = 9 cm

⇒ Side 2 = 4 × 3 = 12 cm

⇒ Side 3 = 5 × 3 = 15 cm

⇒ Since 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225 = 15², it is a right-angled triangle.

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 9 × 12

⇒ Area = 9 × 6 = 54 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 54 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron's Formula

For any triangle with sides a, b, and c, Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)], where s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25). Multiples of these also form triplets.

Semi-Perimeter (s)

In this case, s = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 cm. Area = √[18 × (18−9) × (18−12) × (18−15)] = √[18 × 9 × 6 × 3] = 54 cm².

questions.question: The altitude of an equilateral triangle is 15 cm. Find its area and perimeter.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of an equilateral triangle in terms of altitude (h) = h² / √3

⇒ Area = 15² / √3 = 225 / √3 = 75√3 cm²

Side (a) = 2h / √3 = 30 / √3 = 10√3 cm

Perimeter = 3 × a = 3 × 10√3 = 30√3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is Area = 75√3 cm², Perimeter = 30√3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Altitude (h) = 15**Formula Used:**

Altitude (h) = (√3 / 2) × side (a)

Area = (√3 / 4) × a²

Perimeter = 3 × a

**Calculations:**

⇒ 15 = (√3 / 2) × a

⇒ a = (15 × 2) / √3

⇒ a = 30 / √3 = 10√3 cm

⇒ Area = (√3 / 4) × (10√3)²

⇒ Area = (√3 / 4) × (100 × 3)

⇒ Area = (√3 / 4) × 300 = 75√3 cm²

⇒ Perimeter = 3 × 10√3 = 30√3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is Area = 75√3 cm², Perimeter = 30√3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equilateral Triangle Properties

All sides are equal (a) and all internal angles are 60°. The altitude, median, and angle bisector are the same line segment.

Inradius and Circumradius

Inradius (r) = a / (2√3) = h / 3 and Circumradius (R) = a / √3 = 2h / 3. The ratio R : r is always 2 : 1.

Area-Altitude Relation

Area can be directly calculated from altitude as Area = h² / √3 or Area = (h²√3) / 3.

 J1 has honey and water in the ratio 3:1 .

A quantity of the mixture is transferred from J1 to J2 . After the transfer, the ratio of honey to water in J2 becomes 1:1 . What is the volume of the mixture (in ml) transferred from J1 to J2 ?

questions.question: A square sheet of metal is cut into 4 equal square pieces. If the original sheet had an area of 456 { cm}² , find the side of each smaller square.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Side of smaller square = √(Original Area ÷ Number of pieces)

Side = √(456 ÷ 4)

Side = √114 ≈ 10.68 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10.68 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of the original square sheet = 456 cm²

The sheet is cut into 4 equal square pieces.

Area of a square = side × side = (side)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of each smaller square = Total Area ÷ 4

⇒ Area of smaller square = 456 ÷ 4 = 114 cm²

⇒ Let the side of each smaller square be 's'.

⇒ s² = 114

⇒ s = √114

⇒ s ≈ 10.677 cm

⇒ s ≈ 10.68 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10.68 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Area and Side Relationship

The side of a square is the square root of its area (s = √A). If the area increases by a factor of k, the side increases by a factor of √k.

Diagonal of a Square

The diagonal of a square is s × √2. For the smaller square in this problem, diagonal ≈ 10.68 × 1.414 ≈ 15.10 cm.

Perimeter Calculation

The perimeter of a square is 4 × side. The perimeter of each smaller square is 4 × 10.68 ≈ 42.72 cm.

questions.question: (8(1.75)³ + 1)/((3.5)² - 2.5) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The expression follows the algebraic form: (a³ + b³) ÷ (a² − ab + b²) = a + b.

Rewrite 8 × (1.75)³ as (2 × 1.75)³ = (3.5)³.

Denominator (3.5)² − 2.5 matches (a² − ab + b²) where a = 3.5 and b = 1.

Required value = a + b = 3.5 + 1 = 4.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: [8(1.75)³ + 1] ÷ [(3.5)² − 2.5]

Formula used: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)

⇒ 8 × (1.75)³ + 1 = (2)³ × (1.75)³ + 1 = (2 × 1.75)³ + 1³ = (3.5)³ + 1³

⇒ (3.5)² − 2.5 = (3.5)² − 3.5 + 1 = (3.5)² − (3.5 × 1) + 1²

⇒ Expression = [(3.5 + 1){(3.5)² − (3.5 × 1) + 1²}] ÷ [(3.5)² − 3.5 + 1]

⇒ Expression = 3.5 + 1 = 4.5

**∴ The correct answer is 4.5.**

questions.question: What is the unit digit of 562 times 841 times 927 ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the unit digit of a product, multiply only the unit digits of each number.

Unit digits of 562, 841, and 927 are 2, 1, and 7 respectively.

Product of unit digits = 2 × 1 × 7 = 14.

The unit digit of 14 is 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expression: 562 × 841 × 927

⇒ Unit digit of 562 = 2

⇒ Unit digit of 841 = 1

⇒ Unit digit of 927 = 7

⇒ The unit digit of (562 × 841 × 927) is the unit digit of (2 × 1 × 7)

⇒ 2 × 1 × 7 = 14

⇒ The unit digit of 14 is 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Digit Multiplication Rule

The unit digit of any product depends only on the unit digits of the numbers being multiplied. If the product of unit digits is a multi-digit number, the unit digit of that result is the final answer.

Unit Digit of Powers (Cyclicity)

Unit digits of powers repeat in cycles of 1, 2, or 4. For example, digits 0, 1, 5, and 6 always result in themselves as the unit digit for any positive power n.

Special Case for 5 and Even Numbers

In a series of multiplication, if there is a number ending in 5 and at least one even number, the unit digit of the final product will always be 0.

questions.question: The average of five numbers is 38 . If one number is removed, then the average becomes 30 . What is the removed number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial average of 5 numbers = 38

New average of 4 numbers = 30 (Decrease of 8 per number)

Removed value = Old Average + (Change in Average × Number of remaining items)

Removed value = 38 + (8 × 4) = 38 + 32 = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/44fc20a7f6a4f5c4f9146695b2479ab7495e388bef04562aba97df766c61f8d2.png] 

Given:

Average of 5 numbers = 38

Average of 4 numbers = 30

Formula used:

Sum = Average × Number of observations

Calculations:

⇒ Sum of 5 numbers = 5 × 38 = 190

⇒ Sum of 4 numbers = 4 × 30 = 120

⇒ Removed number = Sum of 5 numbers − Sum of 4 numbers

⇒ Removed number = 190 − 120

⇒ Removed number = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Concept

The average (arithmetic mean) is the sum of all values divided by the total number of values: Average = Total Sum ÷ Count.

Effect of removing a number

If the removed number is greater than the average, the new average will decrease. If the removed number is less than the average, the new average will increase.

Weighted Average

When combining two groups, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question: The solute-like component or the dispersed particles in a colloid form the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**dispersed phase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **colloid** is a **heterogeneous mixture** in which one substance of microscopically dispersed insoluble particles is suspended throughout another substance.
 
• The **solute-like component** or the **dispersed particles** in a colloid form the **dispersed phase**. It represents the **discontinuous phase** of the system.
 
• The component in which the **dispersed phase** is suspended is known as the **dispersing medium** (or **dispersion medium**). It is analogous to the **solvent** in a true solution and is also called the **continuous phase**.
 
• Colloidal particles have a size ranging between **1 nanometer (nm)** and **1000 nanometers (nm)**. They are large enough to scatter light but small enough to remain suspended without settling.
 
• While a **solution** is a **homogeneous mixture** where the solute completely dissolves in the solvent, a **colloid** remains **heterogeneous** even if it appears uniform to the naked eye.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Colloids:** Colloids are classified based on the state (**solid, liquid, or gas**) of the **dispersed phase** and the **dispersion medium**.

 
 
• **Aerosol:** **Liquid or solid** dispersed in **gas** (e.g., **fog, clouds, smoke**).
 
• **Foam:** **Gas** dispersed in **liquid** (e.g., **shaving cream, whipped cream**).
 
• **Emulsion:** **Liquid** dispersed in **liquid** (e.g., **milk, face cream, hair cream**).
 
• **Sol:** **Solid** dispersed in **liquid** (e.g., **milk of magnesia, mud, paints**).
 
• **Gel:** **Liquid** dispersed in **solid** (e.g., **jelly, cheese, butter**).
 
 
 
• **Tyndall Effect:** This is the **scattering of a beam of light** by **colloidal particles**. Because the particles in the **dispersed phase** are large enough, they reflect light, making the path of the beam visible. This effect is not seen in **true solutions** because the solute particles are too small.
 
• **Brownian Motion:** Colloidal particles exhibit a **continuous zigzag motion** called **Brownian motion**. This movement is caused by the **unbalanced bombardment** of the particles of the **dispersed phase** by the molecules of the **dispersion medium**.
 
• **Stability:** Colloids are quite **stable**. Unlike **suspensions** (where particles are **greater than 1000 nm**), the particles in the **dispersed phase** of a colloid do not settle down when left undisturbed for a long period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Solvent (Option 1):** This term is specifically used for **true solutions** (homogeneous mixtures) to describe the component present in the **larger amount** that dissolves the solute. In colloids, the equivalent term is the **dispersion medium**.
 
• **Continuous Phase (Option 3):** This is a synonym for the **dispersion medium**. It is the phase that surrounds the dispersed particles. Since the question asks for the "dispersed particles" component, this option is incorrect as it describes the medium instead.
 
• **Solution Phase (Option 4):** This is not a standard scientific term used to describe the internal components of a **colloidal system**. A **solution** consists of a **solute** and a **solvent** on a **molecular or ionic level**.
 
• **Dialysis:** It is a process used for **purifying colloids** by removing **electrolytes** or **crystalloids** through a **semi-permeable membrane**.
 
• **Electrophoresis:** The movement of **colloidal particles** under the influence of an **electric field**, which helps determine the **charge** (positive or negative) carried by the **dispersed phase** particles.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the term Hiranyagarbha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Golden womb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Hiranyagarbha** is a **Sanskrit** word where **"Hiranya"** means **Gold** and **"Garbha"** means **Womb**, **Seed**, or **Egg**. Therefore, it literally translates to the **"Golden Womb"** or **"Golden Egg"**.
 
• In **Vedic philosophy**, it is considered the source of the creation of the **Universe** or the manifested **Cosmos**. It is often referred to as the **"Soul of the Universe"** or **Brahman**.
 
• The **Hiranyagarbha Sukta** is found in the **Rigveda** (**Mandala 10, Hymn 121**). This hymn suggests that in the beginning, there was only the **Golden Embryo**, which was the sole lord of all created beings. ***Hence, the statement regarding its meaning as the "Golden Womb" is correct.***
 
• Historically, **Hiranyagarbha** was also the name of a **Vedic ritual** performed by kings. This ritual was intended to symbolize the **"rebirth"** of the sacrificer, often to claim **Kshatriya** status even if they were not born into that caste.
 
• A famous historical instance involves the **Rashtrakuta** chief **Dantidurga**, who performed the **Hiranyagarbha ritual** at **Ujjain** in the **8th century (753 AD)** to establish his authority and "become" a **Kshatriya**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sacred Fire:**

 
 
• Commonly known as **Agni**, it is a central element in **Hinduism**. It serves as a medium between humans and gods during **Yajnas** (sacrifices). It is not synonymous with **Hiranyagarbha**.
 
 
 
• **Divine Offering:**
 
 
• Known as **Naivedya** or **Ahuti**, these are food or materials offered to a deity during a ritual. While **Hiranyagarbha** involves offerings, the term itself refers to the "Golden Womb."
 
 
 
• **Royal Coronation:**
 
 
• Known as **Rajyabhishek**, this is the formal ceremony of crowning a monarch. While rituals like **Hiranyagarbha** might precede or accompany a rise to power, they are distinct liturgical acts.
 
 
 
• **The Philosophical Concept:**
 
 
• According to the **Matsya Purana**, after the **Mahapralaya** (great dissolution), the universe was in darkness, and then the **Self-existent Being** appeared and created the **Golden Egg**.
 
• In **Advaita Vedanta**, **Hiranyagarbha** is considered the **First-born** or the **Cosmic Mind**, acting as the intermediary between the **Unmanifested Absolute** and the **Visible World**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** In ancient and medieval India, the **Hiranyagarbha ritual** involved the king passing through a **large golden vessel** shaped like a womb. After the completion of the ritual, the golden vessel was broken and distributed among the **Brahmanas**.
 
• **The Deity:** In later **Puranic** literature, **Hiranyagarbha** is frequently identified with **Lord Brahma**, the creator god, who is said to have been born from the **Golden Egg** that floated in the **Primeval Waters**.
 
• **Scientific Parallel:** Some modern scholars and enthusiasts draw parallels between the **Hiranyagarbha** (Golden Egg) concept and the **Big Bang Theory** or the **Cosmic Egg** theory of modern **Astrophysics**, seeing it as an ancient intuition of the universe's origin from a single point.

questions.question: Raziya Sultana was removed from the throne in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1240**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raziya Sultana**, the daughter of **Shams-ud-din Iltutmish**, was the first and only woman sovereign of the **Delhi Sultanate**.
 
• She ascended the throne of **Delhi** in the year **1236**, succeeding her brother **Ruknuddin Firuz**, who was deposed shortly after taking power.
 
• Her reign was characterized by her refusal to be a puppet ruler; she abandoned the traditional **purdah (veil)**, conducted state business in open court, and led her armies into battle.
 
• In **April 1240**, a rebellion led by **Malik Altunia**, the governor of **Bathinda**, resulted in her defeat and removal from the throne. ***Hence, the statement regarding her removal in 1240 is correct.***
 
• Following her removal, the **Turkish nobility** (known as the **Chahalgani** or the Forty) installed her brother, **Muizuddin Bahram Shah**, as the new **Sultan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Succession Struggle:** Although **Iltutmish** nominated **Razia** as his successor before his death in **1236**, the conservative **nobles** initially refused to accept a woman as ruler and instead crowned her brother **Ruknuddin Firuz**.
 
• **Administrative Reforms:** During her short reign of approximately **three and a half years**, she proved to be a capable administrator, issuing **coins** in her own name and establishing schools, academies, and public libraries.
 
• **Conflict with Nobility:** Her appointment of **Jamal-ud-Din Yaqut**, an **Abyssinian slave**, to the high-ranking post of **Amir-i-Akhur** (Master of the Stables) deeply offended the powerful **Turkish nobles**.
 
• **The Battle of Bathinda:** After **Yaqut** was murdered and **Razia** was imprisoned by **Malik Altunia**, she eventually married him to regain her power and attempt to reclaim the throne.
 
• **Final Days:** **Razia** and **Altunia** marched toward **Delhi** but were defeated by the forces of **Bahram Shah**. They were captured and killed near **Kaithal** in **October 1240**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mamluk Dynasty:** **Razia Sultana** belonged to the **Mamluk Dynasty** (also known as the **Slave Dynasty**), which ruled the **Delhi Sultanate** from **1206** to **1290**.
 
• **The Chahalgani:** This was a group of **40 powerful Turkish nobles** created by **Iltutmish** to assist in administration, but they eventually became "king-makers" and were instrumental in **Razia's** downfall.
 
• **Historical Legacy:** **Razia's** reign challenged the **patriarchal norms** of the **13th century**. Historian **Minhaj-i-Siraj** noted that she was endowed with all the qualities befitting a **Sultan**, but her gender was seen as a primary disqualification by the elite of that era.

questions.question: Which of the following five year plan of India was launched after the initiation of structural adjustment policies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eighth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Eighth Five-Year Plan** was launched for the period **1992 to 1997**. It was the first plan to be introduced after the initiation of **Structural Adjustment Policies (SAP)** and the **New Economic Policy** in **1991**.
 
• During the early **1990s**, India faced a severe **Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis**, which led the government to initiate radical economic reforms under the leadership of Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.
 
• The **Structural Adjustment Policies** focused on **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)**. Because of the economic transition and political instability at the center, the **Eighth Plan** could not be launched in **1990**; instead, two **Annual Plans** were implemented between **1990 and 1992**.
 
• The main objective of the **Eighth Five-Year Plan** was the **modernization of industries** and **human resource development**, including the promotion of **employment, education, and public health**.
 
• It marked a shift in the role of the **Planning Commission** from a directive role to an **indicative** one, where the state's role in the economy began to diminish in favor of the **private sector**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Eighth.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951–1956):**

 
 
• This plan was based on the **Harrod-Domar model** and focused primarily on the **agricultural sector** to overcome food shortages resulting from Partition.
 
• It was launched shortly after **Independence** and long before any **Structural Adjustment Policies** were even conceptualized.
 
 
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961):**
 
 
• Known as the **Mahalanobis Plan**, it emphasized **rapid industrialization** and the development of **heavy and basic industries**.
 
• It followed the **Socialist pattern of society** and aimed to increase the **public sector's** dominance in the Indian economy.
 
 
 
• **Third Five-Year Plan (1961–1966):**
 
 
• Also called the **Gadgil Yojana**, its goal was to make the economy **independent and self-active**.
 
• This plan failed significantly due to the **Sino-Indian War (1962)**, the **Indo-Pak War (1965)**, and a severe **drought in 1965-66**, leading to a "Plan Holiday" from **1966 to 1969**.
 
 
 
• **Structural Adjustment Policies (1991):**
 
 
• These were a set of economic reforms suggested by the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** and the **World Bank** as a condition for financial assistance.
 
• The reforms aimed at reducing **fiscal deficits**, **devaluing the Rupee**, and removing **license raj** to make the Indian market more competitive globally.
 
• The **Eighth Plan** achieved a growth rate of **6.8%**, which was higher than the target of **5.6%**, proving the success of the initial reform phase.

questions.question: Which of the following layer of atmosphere helps in radio transmission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thermosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Thermosphere** is the atmospheric layer located directly above the **Mesosphere** and below the **Exosphere**, extending from about **80 kilometers** to **400-600 kilometers** above the Earth's surface.
 
• This layer is fundamental for **radio transmission** because it contains the **Ionosphere**, a region where the air is ionized by solar radiation. This ionization creates a layer of **free electrons** and **ions** that reflect **radio waves** back to the Earth's surface.
 
• By reflecting these waves, the thermosphere enables long-distance **wireless communication**, allowing radio signals to travel beyond the horizon via **skywave propagation**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Thermosphere.***
 
• In the **Thermosphere**, temperatures increase with altitude due to the absorption of highly energetic **solar radiation** (X-rays and UV rays). Temperatures in this region can soar to **1,500 degrees Celsius** or higher.
 
• The **International Space Station (ISS)** and many **low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites** reside in this layer, benefitting from the extremely low density of the air.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Troposphere**:

 
 
• This is the **lowest layer** of the atmosphere, extending from the surface up to an average height of **13 kilometers** (about **18 km** at the equator and **8 km** at the poles).
 
• It contains approximately **75% to 80%** of the atmosphere's total mass and nearly all the **water vapor**.
 
• All **weather phenomena** such as cloud formation, rain, and storms occur in this layer. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect regarding radio transmission.***
 
 
 
• **Stratosphere**:
 
 
• Located above the troposphere, it extends up to **50 kilometers**.
 
• This layer contains the **Ozone Layer**, which protects life on Earth by absorbing harmful **Ultraviolet (UV) rays** from the sun.
 
• The stratosphere is very stable and lacks turbulent weather, making it the preferred layer for **flying commercial jet aircraft**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect regarding radio transmission.***
 
 
 
• **Mesosphere**:
 
 
• This is the **third layer** of the atmosphere, extending from **50 kilometers to 80 kilometers**.
 
• It is the **coldest layer** of the atmosphere, with temperatures reaching as low as **-90 degrees Celsius**.
 
• **Meteors** burn up in this layer upon entering from space due to friction. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect regarding radio transmission.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ionosphere Dynamics**: The **Ionosphere** is not a separate physical layer but a series of regions (D, E, and F layers) within the thermosphere and mesosphere. During the **day**, the F layer splits into two, while at **night**, some layers disappear, which is why **AM radio** reception is often better and travels further after sunset.
 
• **Auroras**: The **Aurora Borealis** (Northern Lights) and **Aurora Australis** (Southern Lights) are primarily observed in the **Thermosphere**. These occur when **charged particles** from the sun collide with gas molecules, causing them to emit light.
 
• **Atmospheric Boundary**: The **Kármán line**, which is internationally recognized as the boundary between the Earth's atmosphere and **outer space**, is located at an altitude of **100 kilometers**, well within the lower part of the **Thermosphere**.

questions.question: The time period between the 6th and 4th centuries BCE is associated with the rise of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magadha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The period between the **6th and 4th centuries BCE** is known for the rise of **Magadha** as the most powerful **Mahajanapada** (great kingdom) in ancient India.
 
• During this era, **Magadha** (located in present-day **Bihar**) emerged as the center of political activity due to its strategic location and abundant natural resources.
 
• Several powerful dynasties governed **Magadha** during this period, including the **Haryanka dynasty**, the **Shishunaga dynasty**, and the **Nanda dynasty**.
 
• The expansion of **Magadha** began under the rule of **Bimbisara** and his son **Ajatashatru**, who employed both matrimonial alliances and aggressive military conquests to enlarge their territory.
 
• By the **4th century BCE**, the **Nanda dynasty** had established a vast empire, which further paved the way for the **Mauryan Empire** under **Chandragupta Maurya**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reasons for Magadha's Dominance:**

 
 
• **Geographical Advantage:** Magadha was surrounded by rivers like the **Ganges**, **Son**, and **Gandak**, which provided water for agriculture and served as efficient routes for trade and transport.
 
• **Natural Resources:** The region had rich deposits of **iron ore** in the **Rajgir** hills, which allowed for the manufacturing of superior weapons and agricultural tools.
 
• **Military Strength:** Magadha was the first state to use **elephants** on a large scale in warfare, which gave them a significant advantage over rival kingdoms.
 
• **Capital Cities:** The first capital was **Rajgriha** (modern-day Rajgir), a fortified settlement, which was later shifted to **Pataliputra** (modern-day Patna) to better control riverine trade.
 
 
 
• **Other Eras mentioned in the options:**
 
 
• The **Gupta Empire** rose much later, ruling from the **4th to the 6th century CE**, often described as the **Golden Age of India**.
 
• The **Lodi Dynasty** was an Afghan dynasty that ruled the **Delhi Sultanate** from **1451 to 1526 CE**.
 
• The **Mughal Empire** was established in **1526 CE** by **Babur** and lasted until the mid-**19th century**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **6th century BCE** is considered a major turning point in early Indian history, characterized by the emergence of **early states**, **cities**, and the growing use of **iron**.
 
• This period also witnessed the rise of new philosophical and religious movements, most notably **Buddhism** and **Jainism**, which challenged the existing **Vedic** social order.
 
• Out of the **16 Mahajanapadas** mentioned in **Buddhist** and **Jaina** texts (such as the **Anguttara Nikaya**), **Magadha** eventually overshadowed others like **Vatsa**, **Avanti**, and **Kosala** to become the supreme power in Northern India.
 
• The transition from **Janapadas** (small tribal settlements) to **Mahajanapadas** (large territorial states) signifies the evolution of complex socio-political structures in the **Indo-Gangetic plain**.

questions.question: In Humans, involuntary actions including blood pressure, salivation and vomiting are controlled by the ________ in the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Medulla, hind-brain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human brain is divided into three main parts: the **fore-brain**, **mid-brain**, and **hind-brain**. **Involuntary actions** such as **blood pressure**, **salivation**, and **vomiting** are controlled by the **medulla** (or **medulla oblongata**) which is located in the **hind-brain**.
 
• The **medulla oblongata** acts as the primary control center for autonomic functions. It regulates the **Autonomic Nervous System**, which manages internal organ functions without conscious effort. ***Hence, the statement regarding the medulla in the hind-brain is correct.***
 
• The **medulla** contains vital centers for **cardiac**, **respiratory**, and **vasomotor** functions. This means it manages **heart rate**, **breathing**, and the **dilation** or **constriction** of blood vessels to maintain **blood pressure**.
 
• Reflex actions like **vomiting**, **salivation**, **sneezing**, **coughing**, and **swallowing** are also coordinated by the **medulla**.
 
• Structurally, the **medulla** is the lowest part of the brain and serves as a transition point between the brain and the **spinal cord**, facilitating the transmission of signals between the two.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fore-brain (Prosencephalon):**

 
 
• This is the largest and most complex part of the brain, consisting primarily of the **cerebrum**, **thalamus**, and **hypothalamus**.
 
• The **cerebrum** is responsible for high-level functions such as **thinking**, **reasoning**, **memory**, **willpower**, and **voluntary actions**.
 
• The **hypothalamus** regulates **body temperature**, **hunger**, **thirst**, and **emotions**.
 
 
 
• **Mid-brain (Mesencephalon):**
 
 
• It is a small region that connects the **fore-brain** to the **hind-brain**.
 
• It plays a crucial role in **visual** and **auditory processing** and controls **eye movement** and **pupil size**.
 
 
 
• **Hind-brain (Rhombencephalon):**
 
 
• Besides the **medulla**, it contains the **cerebellum** and the **pons**.
 
• The **cerebellum** is responsible for maintaining **posture**, **equilibrium**, and **body balance**. It ensures the **precision** of voluntary movements, such as walking in a straight line or picking up a pencil.
 
• The **pons** acts as a bridge between various parts of the brain and assists in regulating **respiration**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Brainstem:** This structure is formed by the **mid-brain**, **pons**, and **medulla oblongata**. It is essential for life because it controls the flow of messages between the brain and the rest of the body.
 
• **Voluntary vs. Involuntary:** **Voluntary actions** (like walking or talking) are primarily controlled by the **cerebrum** and **cerebellum**, whereas **involuntary actions** (like **heartbeat** or **digestion**) are managed by the **medulla** and the **mid-brain**.
 
• **Biological Significance:** Because the **medulla** controls critical **life-sustaining** functions, any severe injury to this part of the **hind-brain** usually results in immediate **death** due to respiratory or cardiac failure.
 
• **Evolutionary Aspect:** The **hind-brain** is often called the "primitive brain" or "reptilian brain" because it governs the basic survival functions found in almost all vertebrates.

• The **International Space Station (ISS)** is a large-scale modular space station located in **low Earth orbit (LEO)**. It serves as a habitable artificial satellite and a major international research facility.
 
• The launch of the first component of the ISS took place on **November 20, 1998**. • Continuous human presence on the **ISS** began on **November 2, 2000**, with the arrival of **Expedition 1**. Since then, the station has never been without a crew.

questions.question: A ______ is a disturbance that moves through a medium when the particles of the medium set neighbouring particles into motion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**wave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **wave** is a **disturbance** that travels through a **medium**, transferring **energy** from one location to another without the permanent transfer of **mass**.
 
• When a wave moves through a medium, the **particles** of that medium do not travel along with the wave; instead, they **oscillate** or vibrate about their **fixed mean positions**.
 
• The process occurs when a vibrating particle sets its **neighboring particles** into **motion** through **intermolecular forces** or collisions, thereby propagating the disturbance further.
 
• This **energy transport** mechanism is fundamental to all types of **mechanical waves**, such as **sound waves** in air or **seismic waves** in the Earth's crust.
 
• The **medium** can be a **solid**, **liquid**, or **gas**, and its physical properties like **density** and **elasticity** determine the speed at which the wave travels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Waves:**

 
 
• **Longitudinal Waves**: In these waves, the particles of the medium vibrate **parallel** to the direction of wave propagation. A common example is **sound waves**, which consist of **compressions** (high pressure) and **rarefactions** (low pressure).
 
• **Transverse Waves**: In these waves, the particles vibrate **perpendicular** to the direction of wave movement. Examples include **water waves** and **light waves**.
 
 
 
• **Wave Parameters:**
 
 
• **Frequency**: This refers to the **number of oscillations** or cycles per unit of **time**. It is measured in **Hertz (Hz)**. While frequency is a characteristic of a wave, it is not the disturbance itself.
 
• **Wavelength**: The distance between two consecutive points in the same phase, such as from **crest to crest** or **trough to trough**.
 
• **Amplitude**: The **maximum displacement** of the particles of the medium from their **original undisturbed position**. It represents the **energy** or **intensity** of the wave.
 
 
 
• **Wave Speed**: The speed (**v**) of a wave is calculated by the product of its **frequency (f)** and **wavelength**. The formula is expressed as **v = f × wavelength**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Phase**: It describes the **position** and **direction** of motion of a particle at a specific **instant of time** within a cycle. Points in the same phase are at the same stage of their vibration.
 
• **Tone**: In the context of sound, a **tone** is a sound of a **distinct pitch** and **quality**, often resulting from a **single frequency** or a combination of **harmonics**.
 
• **Mechanical vs. Electromagnetic Waves**: Unlike **mechanical waves** (like sound), **electromagnetic waves** (like radio waves or X-rays) do not require a **material medium** and can propagate through a **vacuum** at the **speed of light** (approx **3 × 10⁸ m/s**).
 
• **Acoustics**: The branch of **physics** that deals with the study of mechanical waves in gases, liquids, and solids including **vibration, sound, ultrasound, and infrasound**.

questions.question: The real gross domestic product (GDP) is calculated in a way such that, the goods and services are evaluated at ______.

options.text: prices set by world trade organisation
prices set by International monetary fund
the lowest prices observed in the economy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**some constant set of prices**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Real Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** is an inflation-adjusted measure that reflects the value of all goods and services produced by an economy in a given **year**.
 
• It is calculated by evaluating goods and services at **some constant set of prices**, which are prices from a predetermined **base year**.
 
• By using **constant prices**, the effect of **inflation** or **deflation** is removed, allowing for a comparison of the **actual volume** of production between different time periods.
 
• The primary purpose of calculating **Real GDP** is to track the **true growth** of the economy. If **Real GDP** increases, it signifies that the economy is producing more goods and services, rather than just selling the same amount at higher prices.
 
• In contrast, **Nominal GDP** evaluates production at **current market prices**, meaning it can increase simply because prices have risen, even if the **quantity** of output remains the same.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nominal GDP**: This refers to the **GDP** calculated at **current year prices**. It reflects both changes in **output** and changes in **prices**. While it is useful for understanding the current size of the economy, it is not a reliable indicator of **economic growth** over time.
 
• **GDP Deflator**: It is an economic metric that converts **Nominal GDP** into **Real GDP**. It is a measure of the level of prices of all new, domestically produced, final goods and services in an economy. The formula is: **(Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100**.
 
• **Base Year**: This is the benchmark year against which **economic data** is compared. In **India**, the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** currently uses **2011-2012** as the **base year** for calculating **GDP**.
 
• **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)**: While **Real GDP** measures internal growth, **PPP** is used to compare the **economic productivity** and **standard of living** between countries by adjusting for the **cost of living** and **inflation rates**.
 
• **National Statistical Office (NSO)**: In **India**, the **NSO** is the nodal agency responsible for the release of **GDP** estimates. It operates under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of International Organizations**: Agencies like the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** and the **World Trade Organization (WTO)** monitor global **GDP** trends, but they do not set the prices for a country's internal **Real GDP** calculation. Each country determines its own **base year** and **constant price** metrics.
 
• **Comparison of Real vs. Nominal**: If an economy has high **inflation**, the **Nominal GDP** will be significantly higher than the **Real GDP**. If **Real GDP** is higher than **Nominal GDP**, it indicates **deflation** relative to the **base year**.
 
• **Formula for Real GDP**: It can be derived as **Real GDP = Nominal GDP / (Price Index / 100)**. This allows researchers to isolate the **quantity** factor from the **price** factor.
 
• **Use in Policy**: **Central Banks**, such as the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, use **Real GDP** data to formulate **monetary policy**, adjust **interest rates**, and manage **inflation targets**.

questions.question: In the context of Privatisation, what is the meaning of total decentralisation?

options.text: It implies 100% transfer of ownership of a public enterprise to private sector.
It implies 51% transfer of ownership of a private enterprise to public sector.
It implies 51% transfer of ownership of a public enterprise to private sector.
It implies 100% transfer of ownership of a private enterprise to public sector.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It implies 100% transfer of ownership of a public enterprise to private sector.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Privatisation** is the process of involving the **private sector** in the ownership or operation of a **state-owned enterprise**. It can take several forms, ranging from partial **disinvestment** to complete **denationalization**.
 
• In the context of the question, **total decentralisation** (or total privatisation) refers to the **100% transfer** of **ownership** and **management control** of a **public sector enterprise** to **private hands**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The transfer of ownership from a **private enterprise** to the **public sector** is known as **Nationalisation**. If **51%** or more is transferred to the government, the government gains **majority control**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The transfer of **51% ownership** of a **public enterprise** to the **private sector** is known as **Strategic Disinvestment** or **Majority Privatisation**. In this case, the government might still hold a minority stake, but management control is usually transferred. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• A **100% transfer** of a **private enterprise** to the **public sector** is the absolute form of **Nationalisation**, where the **state** takes full **monopoly** over the industry or specific firm. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The ultimate goal of **total privatisation** is to remove **government interference** entirely from the commercial operations of the entity, allowing **market forces** to dictate efficiency and pricing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **LPG Reforms (1991):** India introduced **Privatisation** as part of the **New Economic Policy** in **July 1991**. The **Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation (LPG)** model was launched by then-Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh** to address the **Balance of Payments (BoP)** crisis.
 
• **Disinvestment:** This refers to the **dilution** of the **Government of India's** stake in **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)**. It is categorized into **Minority Disinvestment** (where the government retains **51%** or more stake) and **Strategic Disinvestment** (where the government sells a significant portion, often **50%** or more, and transfers management control).
 
• **DIPAM:** The **Department of Investment and Public Asset Management**, under the **Ministry of Finance**, is the nodal agency responsible for managing **government investments** in **equity** and advising on the **disinvestment** process.
 
• **Modes of Privatisation:**
 
 
• **Denationalization:** Total **100% transfer** of ownership.
 
• **Joint Venture:** Partial transfer where both **public** and **private** sectors co-exist.
 
• **Franchising:** The government grants the right to a private firm to provide a specific service for a **fixed period**.
 
 
 
• **Objectives:** The primary motives include **improving financial discipline**, facilitating **modernization**, reducing the **fiscal burden** on the **Exchequer**, and promoting **consumer-centric** services through healthy **competition**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Navratnas and Maharatnas:** To ensure that **PSUs** can compete even without full privatisation, the government granted **financial autonomy** to certain profit-making enterprises. **Maharatna** status, introduced in **2010**, gives the highest level of **investment freedom** (up to **5,000 crore**) to top-performing companies like **ONGC**, **NTPC**, and **SAIL**.
 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 1956:** Before **1991**, India followed a policy of **expansion** of the **public sector**, where **17 industries** were exclusively reserved for the **state**. The **1991 reforms** drastically reduced this number to encourage **private participation**.

questions.question: Which book of poems was written by Sarojini Naidu and published in 1905?

__
 
• **The Golden Threshold** is a famous collection of poems written by **Sarojini Naidu** and was first published in **1905** in **London**.
 
• This volume marked her debut in the literary world and established her reputation as a major poet, eventually earning her the title of the **"Nightingale of India"** (**Bharat Kokila**).
 
• The book is divided into three sections: **Folk Songs**, **Songs for Music**, and **Poems**. It features iconic poems like **"Palanquin Bearers"**, **"Coromandel Fishers"**, and **"The Bazaars of Hyderabad"**.
 
• The introduction to the **1905** edition was written by **Arthur Symons**, a renowned British poet and critic, who praised the authentic Indian essence of her work.
 
• The title of the book, **The Golden Threshold**, is also the name of the residence of **Sarojini Naidu** in **Hyderabad**, which is now a center for arts and communication under the **University of Hyderabad**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Indian War of Independence**:

 
 
• This book was authored by **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar** (**V.D. Savarkar**) in **1909**.
 
• It provided a nationalist interpretation of the **Revolt of 1857**, describing it as the **"First War of Indian Independence"** rather than a mere sepoy mutiny.
 
• The book was **banned** by the **British authorities** even before its publication due to its revolutionary content.
 
 
 
• **The Story of My Deportation**:
 
 
• This book was written by the prominent nationalist leader **Lala Lajpat Rai**, popularly known as **Punjab Kesari**.
 
• Published in **1908**, it narrates his experiences and observations during his imprisonment and exile in **Mandalay**, **Burma**, following his arrest in **1907**.
 
 
 
• **Glimpses of World History**:
 
 
• Written by **Jawaharlal Nehru**, this work is a collection of **196 letters** written to his daughter, **Indira Gandhi**, between **1930** and **1933** from various prisons.
 
• It was published in **1934** and provides a broad, secular, and interconnected view of human history from ancient times to the early **20th century**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sarojini Naidu** was born on **February 13, 1879**, in **Hyderabad**. Her birthday is celebrated as **National Women's Day** in **India**.
 
• She was a trailblazer in Indian politics, becoming the **first Indian woman** to serve as the **President** of the **Indian National Congress** at the **Kanpur Session** in **1925**.
 
• Following India's independence in **1947**, she was appointed as the **Governor** of the **United Provinces** (now **Uttar Pradesh**), making her the **first woman** to hold the office of **Governor** in independent **India**.
 
• Other significant literary works by her include **The Bird of Time** (**1912**), **The Broken Wing** (**1917**), and the posthumously published **The Feather of the Dawn** (**1961**).
 
• She was a key participant in the **Salt Satyagraha** of **1930** and led the protest at the **Dharasana Salt Works** alongside other leaders.

questions.question: Ekattarso Mahadeva Temple is also known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chausath Yogini Temple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chausath Yogini Temple**, located in **Morena district, Madhya Pradesh**, is also famously known as the **Ekattarso Mahadeva Temple**.
 
• The name **"Ekattarso Mahadeva"** is derived from the presence of **71 small shrines** within the temple complex. Specifically, it contains **64 chambers** dedicated to the **Yoginis** and a central shrine, along with others, dedicated to **Lord Shiva**.
 
• It was constructed in the **14th century**, specifically around **1323 AD**, during the reign of **King Devapala** of the **Kachchhapaghata dynasty**.
 
• The temple is unique for its **circular structure** and is one of the few well-preserved **hypaethral** (open-to-the-sky) temples in India. It stands on a hill about **100 feet** high in **Mitaoli village**.
 
• It is widely believed by architectural historians that this temple served as the design inspiration for the **old Parliament House (Sansad Bhavan)** in **New Delhi**, which was designed by British architects **Edwin Lutyens** and **Herbert Baker** in the **1920s**.
 
• The temple is maintained and protected by the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** as a monument of national importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Virupaksha Temple:**

 
 
• Located in **Hampi**, in the **Ballari district** of **Karnataka**, it is a part of the **Group of Monuments at Hampi**, a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• It is dedicated to **Lord Shiva**, known here as **Virupaksha**, the consort of the local goddess **Pampa**.
 
• The temple was built by **Lakkana Dandesha**, a commander under the ruler **Deva Raya II** of the **Vijayanagara Empire**. It is famous for its massive **Gopuram** and **Dravidian architecture**.
 
 
 
• **Somnath Temple:**
 
 
• Situated in **Prabhas Patan** near **Veraval** in **Saurashtra, Gujarat**, it is considered the **first** among the **twelve Jyotirlinga** shrines of **Lord Shiva**.
 
• The temple has been destroyed and reconstructed several times throughout history. The present structure was rebuilt in the **Māru-Gurjara style** (Chalukya style) of Hindu temple architecture and was completed in **May 1951**.
 
• The reconstruction was initiated by **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel** after India's independence.
 
 
 
• **Dilwara Temple:**
 
 
• These are a group of **five Shvetambara Jain temples** located about 2.5 kilometers from the **Mount Abu** settlement in **Rajasthan**.
 
• Built between the **11th and 16th centuries**, they are world-famous for their stunning **marble carvings** and intricate architectural details.
 
• The oldest of these, the **Vimal Vasahi temple**, was built in **1031 AD** by **Vimal Shah**, a minister of the **Chaulukya King Bhima I**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Yogini Temples:**
 
 
• The **Yogini cult** was a **Tantric** tradition that flourished between the **9th and 12th centuries**.
 
• Other notable Chausath Yogini temples are located in **Khajuraho (Madhya Pradesh)**, **Hirapur (Odisha)**, and **Ranipur-Jharial (Odisha)**.
 
• The **circular shape** of these temples is often associated with the **Sri Yantra** or the **Dharmachakra**, representing the cosmic flow of energy.

questions.question: A typical example of early cave architecture is the Lomas Rishi cave in the Barabar Hills of ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lomas Rishi Cave** is a prominent example of early **rock-cut architecture** located in the **Barabar Hills** in the **Jehanabad district** of **Bihar**.
 
• It was constructed during the **Mauryan period** in the **3rd century BCE**, making it one of the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in **India**.
 
• The cave is famous for its **ornamental facade**, which mimics contemporary **wooden architecture** of that era, specifically resembling the front of a thatched-roof hut.
 
• The entrance is decorated with a row of **elephants** in a semi-circular frieze, moving towards **Stupa** symbols, showcasing the early artistic mastery of the **Mauryan** artisans.
 
• This cave represents the formative stage of the **Chaitya arch** (horseshoe arch) that became a defining feature of later **Buddhist** cave temples.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Bihar.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Barabar Caves Group**:

 
 
• The **Barabar Hill Caves** consist of four main caves: **Lomas Rishi**, **Sudama**, **Karan Chaupar**, and **Visva Zopri**.
 
• The **Sudama cave** is considered the earliest in the group, dedicated by **Emperor Ashoka** in the **12th year** of his reign (around **261 BCE**).
 
 
 
• **Ajivika Sect**:
 
 
• Most of these caves were primarily dedicated by the **Mauryan** emperors **Ashoka** and his grandson **Dasharatha** to the **Ajivikas**.
 
• The **Ajivika** was a major heterodox ascetic sect of ancient **India** that competed with **Buddhism** and **Jainism**.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Significance**:
 
 
• A characteristic feature of **Mauryan** caves is the **Mauryan polish**, which gives the interior granite surfaces a mirror-like finish.
 
• This technique reflects the advanced masonry skills developed during the **Mauryan Empire**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nagarjuni Caves**:

 
 
• Located about **2 km** from the **Barabar Hills**, the **Nagarjuni Hills** contain three more caves, including the **Gopi cave**.
 
• Inscriptions found here mention **Dasharatha Maurya**, the grandson of **Ashoka**, confirming the continued royal patronage of the region in the late **3rd century BCE**.
 
 
 
• **Internal Layout**:
 
 
• The **Lomas Rishi cave** consists of two rooms: a large rectangular **hall** (mandapa) and a smaller, circular **inner chamber** (shrine) with a hemispherical roof.
 
• This layout indicates that the cave was used as a **place of worship** and assembly for the **ascetics**.
 
 
 
• **Legacy**:
 
 
• The architectural style of the **Lomas Rishi** facade directly influenced the later **Buddhist Chaitya halls** at sites such as **Ajanta**, **Karle**, and **Kanheri**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding thumri?

I. The thumri is very lyrical in its structure and presentation.

II. Thumri is a love song and hence the textual beauty is very important.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thumri** is a prominent genre of **semi-classical Indian music** that is characterized by its **lyrical structure** and expressive presentation. Unlike the more rigid **Khayal**, it prioritizes the **melodic rendering of words** to evoke specific emotions. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• The genre is fundamentally a **love song**, often revolving around the themes of **romantic longing**, **devotion**, and the **shringara rasa** (the sentiment of love).
 
• Because **Thumri** is centered on emotional expression, the **textual beauty** and the meaning of the lyrics are of paramount importance. The performer uses **musical ornamentations** to highlight the nuances of the poetry. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• The compositions are usually set in **Braj Bhasha**, **Awadhi**, or **Bhojpuri** dialects, which lend a rustic yet sophisticated charm to the **textual content**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both I and II.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origins and History:**

 
 
• **Thumri** rose to significant popularity in the **19th Century** within the **royal courts** of **North India**.
 
• It received immense patronage from **Nawab Wajid Ali Shah**, the last Nawab of **Awadh**, who was himself a great poet and musician under the pen name **'Akhtarpiya'**.
 
 
 
• **Regional Schools (Gharanas):**
 
 
• There are two main styles or **gharanas** of **Thumri**: the **Lucknow Thumri** and the **Benares (Varanasi) Thumri**.
 
• The **Lucknow style** is known for its **grace** and **delicacy**, often linked with the **Kathak** dance tradition.
 
• The **Benares style** is characterized by a **robust** and **earthy** quality, focusing heavily on the **'Bol-Banao'** technique where a single line of text is interpreted in multiple melodic ways.
 
 
 
• **Musical Features:**
 
 
• The **Ragas** used in **Thumri** are generally "light" or **'chhota' ragas** such as **Kafi**, **Khamaj**, **Bhairavi**, **Piloo**, and **Des**.
 
• The common **Taals** (rhythmic cycles) associated with this genre include **Deepchandi**, **Dadra**, **Kaherva**, and **Jat**.
 
• The compositions often depict the **divine love** between **Radha and Krishna**, serving as a metaphor for the human soul's longing for the divine.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Famous Exponents:**

 
 
• Legendary singers like **Girija Devi** (often called the **'Queen of Thumri'**), **Begum Akhtar**, **Shobha Gurtu**, and **Bade Ghulam Ali Khan** have made monumental contributions to this art form.
 
• **Girija Devi** was instrumental in bringing the **Purab Ang Thumri** to the global stage and was awarded the **Padma Vibhushan** in **2016**.
 
 
 
• **Performance Techniques:**
 
 
• **Bol-Banao:** The act of using **musical improvisation** to describe the meaning of the **words (Bol)**.
 
• **Bol-Baant:** The use of **rhythmic variations** and distributions of the **lyrics** within the time cycle.
 
• Traditionally, **Thumri** was accompanied by the **Sarangi** and **Tabla**, though the **Harmonium** is now more commonly used.
